name: How do commercial renovation payments usually work?

mainEntity.name: How do payment schedules usually work for commercial renovation projects?
mainEntity.text: How do payment schedules usually work for commercial renovation projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial renovation payments are usually tied to project milestones so both the owner and contractor have a clear way to track progress. A typical structure may include an initial deposit, followed by progress payments after demolition, rough-ins, inspections, finishes, and final completion. Larger projects may use monthly billing based on percentage of work completed. The details depend on contract terms, project size, and whether special-order materials need to be purchased early. Owners should review payment timing carefully and make sure each draw is tied to visible progress or approved materials. It is also wise to confirm what happens if a milestone is delayed by permit review or hidden site conditions. Clear payment terms protect both sides and reduce disputes. A well-written contract should explain retainage, change orders, and closeout conditions so the final payment is not delayed by unresolved punch-list items.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commercial renovation payments usually follow milestones such as deposit, demolition, rough-in completion, inspections, finish stages, and final closeout. The exact structure depends on contract terms, project size, and progress verification. Owners should avoid paying far ahead of completed work unless the agreement clearly justifies it.
